newsitem.title: DENMARK: EMU can force Danish securities abroad - newsletter.
newsitem.headline: EMU can force Danish securities abroad - newsletter.

text.p: About 50 percent of the entire Danish domestic securities trade could be forced abroad when Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) comes into effect in 1999, a Copenhagen political newsletter said on Monday.

"There remains such great uncertainty about how electronic securities trading will function with EMU that the Danish Securities Centre says that around a half of present trading will maybe not be able to be kept on in Denmark," the Mandag Morgen newsletter wrote.

The newsletter said that if the Danish Securities Centre is cut off from being able to perform its present foreign operations, Denmark will lose any leverage it might have when a joint European finance market is created and this will mean higher domestic interest rates.

Denmark satisfies the EMU convergence criteria but its citizens voted in a 1993 referendum to endorse the Maastricht Treaty on condition that the country did not participate in economic and monetary union.
